utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Brdjanin. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I can hear you, and I can understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. General Talic, good morning to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I can hear you and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. We can have the case called now, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, Joanna Korner, assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Appearances -- good morning to you. Appearances for Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I'm John Ackerman, with Tania Radosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Ackerman. And appearances for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. This is Madam Natasha Fauveau-Ivanovic, assisted by Fabien Masson for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you. So I understand, having received this photocopy from an extract from Blackstone's Criminal Practice, that Mr. Ackerman, I suppose, wants to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No. I just wanted to bring you the actual written version of what I was inartfully trying to explain to you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I thought you were trying to outclass Blackstone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, I couldn't even try to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Ackerman. Are there any preliminaries that we need to debate -- discuss this morning? Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So usher, please, could you bring in the witness. And we are not yet in closed session, so we'll go in closed session now before the witness comes in, and I think we have to bring down or pull down the curtains.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, really it was two matters, one which I suddenly remembered. Your Honour asked Mr. Ackerman yesterday about the protective measures motion, and he was going to give you a reply today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Madam Fauveau had already expressed her no objection yesterday, because actually, since I heard nothing from you this morning, Mr. Ackerman, I just placed it in the tray to be filed awaiting a response from -- which I was expecting from Mr. Ackerman. So we will deal with that straight away, and you will have the decision probably tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Your Honour suggested, and we haven't forgotten that we discussed the matters raised by Mr. Ackerman in terms of how Rule 92 evidence is to 1 be treated. And I think the answer is that Mr. Ackerman is going to prepare something, give it to us, and we'll try and reach an agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That is very practical. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the second matter is literally the matter of timetabling. We had lined up for this week three witnesses. That is the one who's just finished, the one to come, and the one after. Well, I mean, when I say lined up, that was sometime ago. But these three men have all been here for some time now. It's clear from any showing that this witness is going to take the rest of the week, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It is also clear, I think, that the witness afterwards, who's also in closed session, is likely to take quite some time as well. We were originally intending for three shortish, by comparison, witnesses to come next week. Because we have to notify VWS with sufficient notice, I -- at lunchtime -- at the last break today, instructed the person in charge that we wouldn't be needing another three witnesses for next week. Your Honour, I hope that's not going to prove unduly pessimistic. But if in the event we finish the third -- or the one after this witness -- quicker, there are still a number of matters outstanding that we could deal with. For example, the question of the document Variant A and B has raised its head again. So if there's time left over --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But I hope that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I anticipate this witness, as you suggest, Ms. Korner, to keep us busy the whole -- the entire -- the rest of the week for sure. I mean, it's -- I've gone through his statement, and it's going to be a long testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For sure. For sure. I'm not quite sure about the next one, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's made a second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I know. Because I received it --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yesterday. But I haven't been through that second statement as yet. I haven't read it as yet. This one is definitely going to keep us busy the entire week for sure. And I suppose you have been made aware that on Friday the sitting is in the afternoon and not in the morning. I am going to check one thing which has been --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Courtroom II or III?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was told it was probably in Courtroom II, and that was not the understanding that I was given before when I had agreed to shift the sitting to the afternoon. So we will be working in Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I'm happy to say it causes me no problems at all this Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think this is all. No?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is it, as far as we're concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, with regard to the upcoming witnesses, the current one - I'll call Witness 1 - I think it's virtually inevitable that we won't finish with him until probably the close of the session on Monday, which would leave us then three days for Witness 2. And I think the chances are rather slim that we can finish Witness 2 by the close of business on Thursday. And I don't have any problem with that witness coming back after the break to finish cross-examination, but it is a bit burdensome. And I don't know -- I don't know how Your Honours want -- Ms. Korner, I think, is optimistic that we're going to finish with him next week. And the way it looks to me, with this witness, we'll be at least as long as we were with the last one. And if that is the case, I don't think we're going to get through all of these -- both of these by the end of next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We can all try, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think -- I definitely agree that this is going to be a long testimony. However, I hesitate to agree or disagree with what you have just suggested, because I would await to see what type of a witness he is. And he seems to be very much -- although he's sitting down and he's very much on his feet ready to trigger off. So I would wait and see how long it takes him to answer questions, because I have a suspicion that it's not -- he's not going to be very loquacious, but let's see anyway. And then by the end of this week -- or at least by Thursday, we should be in a position to see where we are with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, though, the Witness number 2 has also been here now for a week. Even if he has to go part heard over Easter adjournment, I would ask Your Honours -- otherwise, he has to go back again having wasted a week here, and we have to bring up the other witnesses who are shorter on any showing. One is crime based. And I understand from both Mr. Ackerman and Madam Fauveau that the actual killing itself is not going to be disputed. It's the circumstances. So -- but I don't -- I think it would be -- I would ask, even if we don't finish him, that we start the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll play it by the ear and see how it goes, anyway, because I get the suspicion that this witness will -- will be forthcoming without major difficulties. But still it will be a long testimony, I reckon. Okay. So that's it for today. We'll -- I wish you a pleasant afternoon and evening, and we'll meet tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: at 1.45 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 13th day of March, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
